name: Int_x_Substitution_1
questiontext: Evaluate the following integral, using a substitution if necessary: \[ \int {{CT:0}}{{CT:1}}^{{CT:2}}({{CT:1}}^{{CT:0}}-{{CT:3}})^\frac{{CT:4}}{{CT:5}} d{{CT:1}} \] [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Using a substitution, let \[u={{CT:1}}^{{CT:0}}-{{CT:3}}\]

Differentiating \(u\) with respect to {{CT:6}} gives \[du={{CT:0}}{{CT:1}}^{{CT:2}}d{{CT:1}}\]

Therefore

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \int {{CT:0}}{{CT:1}}^{{CT:2}}({{CT:1}}^{{CT:0}}-{{CT:3}})^\frac{{CT:4}}{{CT:5}}\ d{{CT:1}} &\displaystyle = &\displaystyle\int u^{{CT:7}} du \\ &\displaystyle = &\displaystyle {{CT:8}}u^{{CT:9}}+c  \\ &\displaystyle = &\displaystyle {{CT:8}}({{CT:1}}^{{CT:0}}-{{CT:3}})^{{CT:9}}+c \end{array}\]
